title: how the nudge, preguard and recall hooks share per-session state
summary: The PostToolUse nudge, the PreToolUse preguard and the UserPromptSubmit recall hooks on all three hosts share ONE per-session state file, find_nudge_<sid>[_<aid>].json, whose path comes from findNudgeStatePath in hooks/nudge-state-path.mjs (os.tmpdir()). Every write is wrapped in try/catch and never fails the hook, so a bad path disables the nudges silently instead of erroring: the literal /tmp path it replaced meant C:\tmp on Windows, which does not exist on a fresh machine, and the spiral nudge could never fire there.

steps.role: the one place the state path is built
reads/writes seen_find, nonfind_streak etc.; the spiral needs seen_find to persist across calls
reads seen_find_queries from the same file to deny duplicate finds
opens the same file at prompt time (also codex-/cursor- variants)

invariants: Never build this path from a literal /tmp; tests/nudge-state-path.test.ts fails if any hook does
A swallowed state-write failure looks like 'the nudge never fires', not an error
